Name: premature_commitment
Title: Answering Before Knowing: Premature Answer Commitment in Autoregressive LLM Generation
Short Hypothesis: During free-form autoregressive generation, an LLM often commits to an answer token distribution several positions BEFORE its internal retrieval of the relevant fact has completed. We hypothesize that this temporal mismatch—premature commitment—causes a distinct class of errors: the model would have retrieved the fact correctly a few tokens later, but the earlier committed trajectory locks out the correct answer. This gap is (1) measurable by tracking when the answer distribution stabilizes vs. when the fact becomes decodable across generation steps, (2) more severe for facts requiring deeper/later retrieval (e.g., multi-hop), and (3) mitigable by a lightweight 'commitment-delay' decoding intervention.
Related Work: Latent multi-hop work (Yang et al. 2024; Yu et al. 2025 'logit flow'; Liu et al. 2026 'layer-order inversion'; Karmim et al. 2026) studies whether/how facts are composed WITHIN a single forward pass at the final prompt position, using single-token cloze probes. None study the ACROSS-TOKEN temporal dynamics of a multi-token generation: whether an answer's token distribution stabilizes at generation step t before the fact is decodable at step t. Self-consistency and speculative-decoding literature manipulates decoding but not with reference to internal retrieval timing. My own prior proposals address static single-pass residual routing (retrieval-gap), query-form routing, interference, and provenance—none address the sequential decoding-time commitment dynamic. This is the first work to define and measure a 'retrieve-vs-commit timing gap' across autoregressive positions and to intervene on decoding based on internal retrieval readiness.
Abstract: Autoregressive language models generate answers one token at a time, but the internal retrieval of the fact needed to answer may not finish before the model has already begun committing to a response. We hypothesize a distinct failure mode—premature answer commitment—in which the model's answer-token distribution stabilizes several generation positions before the relevant fact becomes internally decodable, causing errors even when the fact is retrievable a few steps later. We operationalize two per-example, per-position signals during free-form generation: (i) commitment time, the earliest generation step at which the top answer candidate's probability stabilizes (crosses a threshold and stops changing), and (ii) retrieval time, the earliest step at which the correct answer becomes linearly decodable from intermediate activations via logit lens/probes. Their difference defines a retrieve-vs-commit gap. We measure this gap across factual, relational, and 2-hop questions asked in open-ended (non-cloze) form, and test whether negative gaps (commit-before-retrieve) predict errors better than a difficulty baseline. We causally validate via activation patching: injecting the late-retrieved fact direction at the earlier committed positions to test whether errors reverse. Finally, we introduce a training-free 'commitment-delay' decoding intervention: we detect low internal retrieval readiness at the answer position and insert a short deliberation buffer (e.g., a learned pause token or brief re-encoding) before committing, measuring accuracy gains, recovery of premature-commitment errors, and side effects on already-correct answers. Experiments span Pythia, Qwen2.5, and Llama-3 across scales.
Experiments: 1) DATASET: ~4k questions posed in OPEN-ENDED generation form (not cloze), spanning factual (single-hop), relational, and 2-hop compositional queries where the answer is a multi-token entity. Include paraphrases and a distractor-context variant. Restrict causal analyses to items whose constituent facts are individually retrievable (verified via single-hop probes) to isolate commitment from knowledge absence. 2) TIMING SIGNALS: During greedy/temperature generation, at each generation step t compute (a) COMMITMENT time: earliest t where the model's probability on the eventual top answer entity stabilizes (probability > threshold and change < epsilon for k consecutive steps); (b) RETRIEVAL time: earliest t where the correct answer token/entity is linearly decodable from mid/late-layer residuals at that position via logit lens and a trained probe. Define Gap = CommitmentTime - RetrievalTime (negative = premature commitment). 3) PREDICTIVE TEST: Test whether negative Gap predicts final-answer errors; report AUROC and incremental AUROC over a difficulty-only baseline (answer frequency, prompt length, isolated-recall logit margin). Compare Gap distributions for single-hop vs multi-hop (prediction: multi-hop retrieves later, larger premature-commit gap). 4) CAUSAL VALIDATION: For premature-commit error cases, use activation patching to inject the answer-position retrieval direction (extracted from the later step where the fact IS decodable, or from a correct-generation run) into the earlier committed positions; measure whether the correct answer is restored, vs random-direction control. 5) COMMITMENT-DELAY INTERVENTION: Training-free decoder that, at the answer-onset position, estimates internal retrieval readiness (probe confidence); if below threshold, inserts a short deliberation buffer—options: (a) append a pause/'let me think' filler token and re-run, (b) re-encode with a brief self-generated scratch step, (c) delay commitment by sampling a low-content continuation and re-scoring. Measure: recovery rate on premature-commit errors, accuracy gain overall, false-intervention rate on already-correct answers (must not degrade), and latency cost. Baselines: no intervention, always-CoT, self-consistency, and a fixed random-delay control (to show gains come from readiness-targeting, not extra compute alone). 6) GENERALIZATION/SCALING: Repeat on Pythia (1.4B/6.9B), Qwen2.5 (0.5B/7B), Llama-3 (8B); report whether the premature-commit gap and intervention gains shrink or grow with scale. METRICS: retrieve-vs-commit Gap distributions, predictive/incremental AUROC, causal restoration rate, intervention recovery rate, overall accuracy delta, false-intervention rate, latency overhead, scaling trends.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Defining 'commitment time' via probability stabilization is heuristic; we report robustness across threshold/epsilon settings and validate that stabilized tokens indeed appear in the output. 2) Probe decodability may overstate retrieval; we require causal patching corroboration and treat decodability as necessary-not-sufficient. 3) The premature-commit gap may correlate with generic difficulty; we control via incremental AUROC over a difficulty baseline. 4) The commitment-delay intervention adds compute—we include a matched random-delay control to attribute gains to readiness-targeting rather than extra tokens, and report latency. 5) For multi-hop, commitment errors may entangle with reasoning failures; we restrict causal claims to items with verified constituent-fact retrievability. 6) Effects may be architecture/scale specific; we characterize across families rather than assume universality. 7) In free-form generation, answer position identification is noisier than in cloze; we use entity-span detection and analyze aggregate statistics.
